data.title: Mission Valley Bancorp Reports Third Quarter Results
data.description:
Mission Valley Bancorp (, “Mission Valley”, or the “Company”) announced today net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $2.1 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $3.8 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, compared to net income of $4.9 million, or $1.45 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Tamara Gurney, Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We are pleased with the year-to-date growth of $15.2 million, or 10.1% annualized, in our non-interest bearing core deposits, particularly during a very challenging time to attract and retain core deposits for the industry as a whole. This supported gross loan growth of $6.4 million, after selling $13.4 million in SBA loan principal, for the current quarter. However, the most significant highlight of the quarter was the leadership transition at Mission Valley Bank with Brian Carlson being appointed President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank as I stepped in to the role of Executive Chair and CEO of Mission Valley Bancorp. Brian will be instrumental in shaping the path forward for the Company and the Bank.”

Brian Carlson, President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank and President of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We were able to produce solid net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the quarter despite the impact from the industry-wide headwinds on SBA lending volume and the increase in our provision for credit losses primarily due to one charged-off commercial loan. The quality of our SBA loan portfolio remains strong with low levels of past due, non-accrual, classified loans, and overall default rates that continue to outperform industry averages. In addition, secondary market premiums on SBA loans remain at favorable levels as we continue to grow the SBA loan portfolio, while maintaining our asset quality.”

Mr. Carlson continued, “As we look ahead to the fourth quarter and closing out 2026, we look forward to the full launch of one of our digital transformation initiatives and we will be focused on executing certain strategic and proactive measures with respect to our loan and investment portfolios to reposition and strengthen our balance sheet for 2027 and beyond.”

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Net Income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Net Interest Income was $8.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $0.5 million, or 7.01%, compared to the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net Interest Margin was 4.47% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 4.54% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-Interest Income was $2.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $0.5 million, or 17.98%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. Non-Interest Income includes gain on sale of loans and the change in the fair value of Small Business Administration (“SBA”) servicing assets.
  • $13.4 million in loan principal sold resulting in gain on sale of $0.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $17.9 million in loan principal sold and gain on sale of $0.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Change in the fair value of SBA servicing assets resulted in a net loss of $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net gain of $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Balance Sheet Highlights

  • Total Assets were $790.2 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $29.8 million, or 3.92%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Gross Loans were $637.1 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $27.5 million, or 4.51%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total Deposits were $648.4 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $12.9 million, or 2.03%, compared to December 31, 2025. The $12.9 million growth in Total Deposits was driven by the $15.2 million increase in non-interest bearing deposits, partially offset by the $2.3 million decrease in interest bearing deposits.

Asset Quality

  • $397 thousand in net charge-offs on loans in the third quarter of 2026 primarily from one commercial loan, compared to $60 thousand in net recoveries from previously charged-off loans in the third quarter of 2025.
  • $13.0 million in Non-Accrual Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $9.2 million in Non-Accrual Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Non-Accrual Loans were comprised of $6.3 million from commercial loans, $4.8 million from accounts receivable loans, and $1.9 million from SBA loans.
  • $33.1 million in Classified Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $16.7 million in Classified Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Classified Loans were comprised of $15.4 million from accounts receivable loans, $8.4 million from commercial loans loans, $7.5 million from real estate loans, and $1.8 million from SBA loans.
  • $10.5 million in Past Due Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $15.6 million in Past Due Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Past Due Loans were comprised of $5.2 million from commercial loans, $4.8 million from accounts receivable loans, and $0.5 million from SBA loans.
  • Provision for Credit Losses was $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The provision in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by the charge-off of one commercial loan.
  • The Allowance for Credit Losses was $8.4 million, or 1.32% of Gross Loans, as of September 30, 2026, compared to $8.1 million, or 1.33% of Gross Loans, as of December 31, 2025.

Capital and Liquidity

  • Capital position remains strong, which is reflected by Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio of 10.31%, Tier 1 Capital ratio of 11.14%, Total Risk Based Capital Ratio of 12.33%, and Leverage Ratio of 10.07%.
  • Available borrowing capacity of $214.3 million as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of $9.0 million, or 4.03%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Unpledged available-for-sale investment securities of $40.3 million as of September 30, 2026.

About Mission Valley Bancorp

Mission Valley Bancorp is a bank holding company headquartered in Sun Valley, California with two wholly owned subsidiaries Mission Valley Bank (the "Bank") and Mission SBA Loan Servicing LLC (“Mission SBA”). The Bank was founded in 2001 and is a full-service, independent, commercial bank specializing in the banking needs of small to medium businesses with full-service branches in the San Fernando, Santa Clarita, and San Gabriel Valleys. Mission SBA is a de novo SBA lender service provider (“LSP”) established in March 2021 that provides SBA lending services to other financial institutions.

data.title: Copper One Completes First Hole of 10,000-Foot Phase 2 Drill Program, Intersecting Visually Identified Native Copper in MHB-39 at Flagship Majuba Hill Project, Nevada
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, BC – October 30, 2026 – TheNewswire - Copper One Resources Corp. ("Copper One") (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of drill hole MHB-39, the first hole of its Phase 2 diamond drilling program of up to 10,000 feet  at its 100%-owned flagship Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project (“Majuba Hill” or the “Project”) in Pershing County, Nevada.

MHB-39 reached a final depth of 1,460 feet (approximately 445 metres), exceeding its originally planned depth of 1,250 feet (381 metres). Persistent silicification prompted the technical team to extend the hole to further evaluate the alteration encountered at depth. Visually identified native copper was observed earlier in the hole.

MHB-39 Highlights

  • First Phase 2 hole completed: MHB-39 reached 1,460 feet, approximately 210 feet beyond the upper end of its original planned depth range.

  • Native copper (Figure 1) and copper oxides (Figure 2) observed in hole.  These observations remain subject to laboratory confirmation.

  • Persistent silicification: Continued silicification supported extending the hole beyond its original target depth.

Geological observations at final depth: MHB-39 terminated in moderately silicified rhyolite containing stockwork tourmaline veinlets, trace fine-grained pyrite and trace sphalerite

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “Completing MHB-39 beyond its originally planned depth provides our technical team with additional geological information as we advance Phase 2 at Majuba Hill. The visual secondary copper minerals observed in the hole and persistent silicification warrant further evaluation through detailed logging, sampling and analysis. With a program of up to 10,000 feet, we are working to better understand the distribution of mineralization and alteration across our priority targets.”

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 1: Native Copper at a depth of 1,090 feet (332 metres). Visual identification is preliminary and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

MHB-39 Geological Summary

MHB-39 was originally designed to reach a depth of between 1,000 and 1,250 feet. As drilling progressed, persistent silicification led the technical team to extend the hole, which ultimately reached 1,460 feet.

At its final depth, the hole intersected moderately silicified rhyolite with stockwork tourmaline veinlets, trace fine-grained pyrite and trace sphalerite. These observations will be incorporated into the Company’s geological interpretation to help guide subsequent drilling.

Visual mineral observations are preliminary and do not establish metal grades, or economic significance. Laboratory analysis is required to determine copper, silver, gold and other metal concentrations.

The Company’s expanded Phase 2 diamond core drilling program (the “Phase 2 Program”) comprises up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of HQ/PQ diamond core drilling. The Phase 2 Program is intended to accelerate systematic testing of priority targets at Majuba Hill and support the Company’s objective of advancing the Project toward a maiden mineral resource estimate prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). More than 95,000 feet (28,956 metres) have been drilled to date at Majuba Hill across more than 100 drill holes.

Assay results from the completed 2026 Phase 1 drill program remain pending and will be announced once received, reviewed and validated.

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 2: Copper oxides at 820 feet (249 metres) in MHB-39.

Source: CME Group, Copper Futures Overview, last updated September 18, 2026, at 4:49 a.m. CT. Market data is delayed by at least 10 minutes.

Phase 2 Program Highlights

  • Expanded program of up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of diamond core drilling.


  • Initial approximately 5,000 feet (1,524 metres) contracted to Evolve using one portable HQ/PQ core drill.


  • Continuous, two-shift drilling operations planned on a 24-hour-per-day, seven-day-per-week basis.


  • Maximum planned hole depth under the initial scope of approximately 1,700 feet (518 metres), with final collar locations, azimuths, inclinations and depths to be determined by the Company’s technical team.


  • Real-time operational visibility through Evolve’s EVX Connect platform.


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 3: Elevated view of drill pad 26DPH-8 at Copper One Resources Corp.’s 100%-owned Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project in Pershing County, Nevada.

Real-Time Drill Program Technology

As previously announced the Company engaged Evolve Exploration Nevada, LLC (“Evolve”) to undertake the Phase 2 diamond core drilling.

Every Evolve drill rig operates on EVX Connect, Evolve’s real-time operational platform. Through EVX Connect, Copper One expects to receive live drilling metrics, digital PLOD reporting, drill-hole coordinate tracking, streamlined invoicing and high-quality photographs of drill core as it is recovered. Information will be accessible through web and mobile interfaces, providing the Company’s technical and management teams with timely visibility into drilling progress and field operations.

About the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada

Majuba Hill is Copper One Resources Corp.’s flagship copper-silver-gold exploration project, located in Pershing County, Nevada, USA. Nevada ranked first globally on the Investment Attractiveness Index in the Fraser Institute’s Annual Survey of Mining Companies 2025. The property comprises approximately 9,684 acres (3,919 hectares) and is situated approximately 70 miles (113 road kilometres) southwest of Winnemucca and 156 miles (251 kilometres) northeast of Reno.

The project benefits from excellent infrastructure, including year-round road access, nearby electrical power, water, and access to a skilled mining workforce. Majuba Hill is a past-producing copper mine with an extensive exploration database, including approximately 95,000 feet (28,956 metres) of historical drilling, providing a strong technical foundation for ongoing exploration aimed at further defining the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Exploration has outlined a large copper-silver-gold hydrothermal mineralized system that remains open for expansion. Current exploration is focused on advancing the Company's geological model through systematic drilling, geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and structural interpretation to evaluate the scale, continuity, and significance of mineralization. Additional drilling and technical studies will be required to further define the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Larry Segerstrom, M.Sc. (Geology), CPG, a non-independent consulting geologist to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power-system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,786 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. Systematic exploration is continuing to evaluate the scale and continuity of the mineralized system.

In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,704-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

Copper One is advancing its portfolio through systematic exploration, modern geological modelling and disciplined technical evaluation. The Company remains committed to responsible exploration practices, technical transparency and the disciplined advancement of critical-metals projects across North America.

data.title: University Bancorp Closes on the Acquisition of 20% of UIF Corporation for Cash & Stock Worth About $15.2 Million
data.description:
ANN ARBOR, MI / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / University Bancorp, Inc. or ("UNIB") announced that it closed today on the previously announced transaction to acquire 20% of UIF Corporation. UIF is a key subsidiary of University Bank, previously 80% owned, and now 100% owned by University Bank. The final terms at the closing of the transaction were different than the terms originally negotiated, which originally involved an all-stock stock swap.

In the transaction, UNIB issued 482,054 newly issued shares of UNIB common stock and in addition, paid $3,911,147.50 cash, to acquire the 20% of UIF that it did not already own. At September 30, 2026, UIF had shareholders' equity of $76,050,646. Minority Interest of $15,210,129 as of September 30, 2026 was acquired in the transaction. The acquisition therefore increases the shareholders' equity of UNIB by $11,298,981.70 as of September 30, 2026, had it closed then. The Tier 1 Capital of University Bank increases as a result of the acquisition by about $4 million going forward due to the elimination of the minority interest in UIF.

Shareholders and investors are encouraged to refer to the financial information including the investor presentations, audited financial statements, strategic plan and prior press releases, available on our investor relations web page at: http://www.university-bank.com/bancorp/.

About UNIB

Ann Arbor-based University Bancorp is a Federal Reserve regulated financial holding company that owns:

  • 100% of University Bank, a bank based in Ann Arbor, Michigan;
  • 100% of Bank of Whittier, N.A., a bank located in Whittier, California;
  • 100% of Crescent Assurance, PCC, a captive insurance company licensed in Washington DC; and

University Bank together with its Michigan-based subsidiaries, holds and manages a total of over $36 billion in financial assets for over 185,000 customers, and our 550 employees make us the 5th largest bank based in Michigan. University Bank is an FDIC-insured, locally owned and managed community bank, and meets the financial needs of its community through its quality, creative and innovative services. Founded in 1890, University Bank® is the 15th oldest bank headquartered in Michigan. We are proud to have been selected as the "Community Bankers of the Year" by American Banker magazine, as the recipient of the American Bankers Association's Community Bank Award and as the recipient of USA Today's Top Workplace Award for several years in a row. data.title: Lundin Mining Announces Updated Share Capital and Provides Update on Share Buybacks
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- () (Nasdaq Stockholm: LUMI) Lundin Mining Corporation ("Lundin Mining" or the "Company") reports the following updated share capital and voting rights, in accordance with the Swedish Financial Instruments Trading Act.

The number of issued and outstanding shares of the Company has increased by 11,573 to 851,371,131 common shares with voting rights as of October 30, 2026. The increase in the number of issued and outstanding shares from October 1, 2026 to date is a result of the exercise of employee stock options or the vesting of employee share units. During this period, the Company did not purchase any shares for cancelation under its Normal Course Issuer Bid program ("NCIB").

Normal Course Issuer Bid

Under the Company's shareholder distribution policy, the Company is committed to allocating up to US$150 million in annual share buybacks through the NCIB program. The Company's Board of Directors has also approved an increase of up to US$100 million to the share repurchase program for the remainder of 2026. So far during 2026, Lundin Mining has acquired 6,098,494 common shares at an average cost of approximately C$35.70/share.

About Lundin Mining

Lundin Mining is a Canadian mining company headquartered in Vancouver, Canada with three operating mines in Brazil and Chile. We produce metals that underpin global development, supporting infrastructure, electrification, technological innovation, and economic resilience. Our strategic vision is to become a top ten global copper producer. To get there, we are executing a clear growth strategy, which includes advancing one of the world's largest copper, gold, and silver projects in the Vicuña District on the border of Argentina and Chile, where we hold a 50% interest. We also hold a 31% interest in the Los Helados project, located adjacent to our operating Caserones mine, providing longer term growth optionality. Lundin Mining has a proven track record of value creation through resource growth, operational excellence, and responsible development. The Company's shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (LUN) and Nasdaq Stockholm (LUMI). Learn more at www.lundinmining.com.

The information in this release pertaining to the updated share capital and voting rights is subject to the disclosure requirements of Lundin Mining under the Swedish Financial Instruments Trading Act. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out below on October 30, 2026 at 4:30 pm Pacific Time.

For further information, please contact: Stephen Williams, Vice President, Investor Relations: +1 604 806 3074; Robert Eriksson, Investor Relations Sweden: +46 8 440 54 50
